_comment: The bootstrap layer. It declares its directories under `directories` below, because discovery reads declarations rather than walking the tree, and an undeclared directory is not this layer's graph however many files sit in it. FIVE processes live in `processes/` and exactly one of them is an ENTRY POINT: `processes/initialize-harness.bpmn`. A Bootstrapping Agent that has read README.md is at its start event with nowhere else to begin. The other four are SUB-PROCESSES, each reached only by a call activity: `discussion.bpmn` determines which harness and where; `human-agent-discussion.bpmn` is the one reusable way any diagram asks a person anything; `complete-initialization.bpmn` makes sure every step the declarations name is done; `log-message.bpmn` records what a step is doing. The constraint was never 'one file'; it is that there is one place to start. Every harness is composed ON TOP of this rather than being its parent, which is why nothing here may refer to one.

_iriBase_comment: The one place bootstrap's address is written. Every IRI bootstrap mints is derived from it and the MAJOR of `version`: `<iriBase>v<major>/…`, for what a program reads and for pages a person reads alike (owner, 2026-10-23, option "B. Major in address"); the exact release is the pin's, not the address's. A fork changes this line and re-runs the sync; nothing else names the address by hand.
_nodeSchemas_comment: This Knowledge Graph's Node Kinds, declared: every `$schema` value a file here carries, and the Node Schema that defines it. A path is relative to this file; an IRI is a published standard. Declared rather than found by searching `schemas/`, so a reader with nothing installed can go from a file's `$schema` straight to its definition — and a test fails on a file whose `$schema` is not listed here.
_title_comment: The display name. `name` stays the identifier that file names use; `title` is what a person reads.

_directories_comment: Every entry is a subdirectory rather than `bootstrap/` itself. `isSkillMd` is declaration-over-location: a markdown file that does NOT declare `$schema:` is a skill. README.md and AGENTS.md declare neither, so a graph rooted at `bootstrap/` would count this layer's two DECLARED ASSETS as skill nodes — the layer has already said what those files are, and a scan would contradict its own declaration. Keeping the graph one level down means the two mechanisms cannot collide. Declared explicitly rather than relying on DEFAULT_DIRECTORIES: a declaration that exists is honoured as written, so defaults do not apply to a layer that declares anything at all.

stickies.bodyAppend: **Scope:** phase one of two, and valid with NOTHING installed — no skills, no knowledge graph, no MCP, no work-plan store. One process here is the place to start. Everything else is composed on top of it, and nothing here may import from the layer above.

directories.description: The schemas bootstrap is checked against: `graph.schema.json`, the shape of a declaration and the definition of every term bootstrap uses; and the input and output of the discussion Process. Their published `$id`s do not change when a file moves.
bootstrap's four Roles: Bootstrapping Agent, Requestor, Knowledge Graph Data Store and Logger.

bootstrap's Processes: `initialize-harness.bpmn`, the only one an Actor starts; `discussion.bpmn`, which it calls to determine the harness and repositories; `human-agent-discussion.bpmn`, the reusable discussion every diagram calls to ask a person anything; `complete-initialization.bpmn`, which checks every initialization step the declarations name; and `log-message.bpmn`, which any step may call to record what it is doing. `ns.jsonld` defines the elements these diagrams add to BPMN (skill, role, precondition), written with the prefix `bootstrap.processes:`.

Which languages a model is good at, and whether anybody checked. In bootstrap because an agent needs it before any harness is loaded. Read when a session opens, never written by a process: only a person grants a validation.

renderExemption._comment: Owner, 2026-09-20, verbatim: "it is exception to harness/layer not having visualtion/workflow visualizer. but it must have its json/jsonld... that is its existence." Declared here rather than hardcoded in a checker, because a checker that names one layer states a rule true only for the layer somebody remembered. `owes` is required by the schema: an exemption with no substitute is a hole, and bootstrap is not dropping out of the requirement — it is trading a criterion it could fail quietly for one it cannot.
renderExemption.reason: bootstrap is what an agent reads before it knows what a repository is, with nothing installed: no Skills beyond its own, no Knowledge Graph loaded, no server and no Tools. So it renders nothing for a person to browse.
renderExemption.owes: Its own Knowledge Graph, written out as `.jsonld` with a `.json` copy and published at `<base>/bootstrap/bootstrap.jsonld`, the exact address its `@id` names. Governed by `skills/bootstrap-graph-emission.md` and `skills/bootstrap-graph-publication.md`.
renderExemption._reachableAt_comment: Where a person is sent to read about bootstrap, since bootstrap renders no pages of its own: its own README, relative to this directory. The site build publishes bootstrap's files as they sit, with each `.md` also rendered as `.html`, so the link stays inside bootstrap.

_needs_comment: The layer this one sits on. Owner, 2026-09-20: "So bootsteap, cat harness, fa-core, f-a, from bottom to top." Declared rather than hardcoded in the navbar, so the ordering is a fact of the repository and not of whichever consumer needed it first. An EMPTY list is an assertion that this layer sits on nothing — the floor — while an ABSENT one means nobody has said, and the two are different answers.
_builtAtPublish_comment: Owner, 2026-10-14 (B1). This layer's JSON-LD @context is generated at publish by the `jsonld:contexts` writer of the harness that mounts it, from the prefixes and content-context terms its documents use, flattened with the prefix tables of every layer it needs. Those tables are read at the CHECKOUT's pins, not at pins this layer's commit names, so no commit of it can hold the file current: it is built at publish and never committed (bean 63q4). It sits BESIDE the vocabulary, at ns.context.v1.jsonld, not at ns/context/v1.jsonld (owner, 2026-10-15, D1): this layer's namespace is a DOCUMENT, ns.jsonld, staged at the extensionless ns and v<major>/ns, so ns cannot also be the directory a context under ns/context/ needs, and a static host cannot serve both. Named here by its writer's script name and by what it holds only: bootstrap names nothing above it (bean iwtn).

builtAtPublish.reason: the prefixes and content-context terms its documents use, flattened with the jsonldPrefixes of the layers it needs at the checkout's pins
